newsitem.title: UK: Some Eurotunnel services to resume.
newsitem.headline: Some Eurotunnel services to resume.

text.p: Anglo-French Channel tunnel operator Eurotunnel Plc said some single-line services in the tunnel should restart later today, after they were disrupted by a fire, which broke out on a freight shuttle train last night.

The company said the fire, which damaged 15 trucks and the rear locomotive of the train, had caused severe damage and would take an indefinite period for the damaged rail equipment and section of the tunnel to be restored to full working order.
"Single-line services in the tunnel should be resumed later today, first for Eurostars and national network trains, then gradually for Le Shuttle customers."
The company said it aimed to restore two thirds of the normal flow of traffic.
A spokeswoman said some Eurostar passenger services, rail freight and Le Shuttle freight services would be resuming today, but Le Shuttle tourist service would not restart today.

The company said eight truck drivers and crew members suffering from smoke inhalation were treated in the service tunnel before being taken to nearby hospitals for further treatment. They should be discharged later today, it said.

Executive chairman of Eurotunnel Patrick Ponsolle said, "It is a serious accident, the first since operations started in the Channel Tunnel. I am, however, delighted to see that the safety procedures worked well."
